Black Friday and Cyber Monday are the Super Bowl for scammers — and the losses are ugly on both sides of the border.

The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) reports Americans lost about $503 million to online shopping scams — mostly non-delivery and non-payment fraud, where you pay and the package never ships. In Canada, the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre says people reported roughly $351 million in fraud losses in just the first half of 2026.

The trick of the season: a text claiming a “delivery fee” is owed on a package. One shopper who tapped it lost $5,000 in gift cards. The tell is almost always the same — a real retailer or courier never demands payment in gift cards.

My take: if a deal can only be paid with a gift card, it isn't a deal — it's a trap. Slow down, go to the retailer's real site directly, and never pay a “fee” from a text.

Gotten a sketchy “delivery fee” text this week? 👇

Source: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) and Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (Nov. 2026)
Educational only — not financial advice.
